key: I have beheld his strong and secret dwelling, longing have sought the Founder’s habitation. I asked of others, and they said in answer, May we, awakened men, attain to Indra.
s: After the opening question, who has seen Indra, the singer tells of his search; Sāyaṇa, on 5.30.2, reads it as a seeker who asks if Indra, though he exists, is within reach, and, told he is, sees the rest of the hymn.

evidence.gloss: I asked others too, the learned on the way, about Indra. Asked, they told me of Indra. What they said: we, leaders of rites, seeking to know, have attained Indra. The meaning is: though Indra exists, if he is hard to reach he is not to be approached; wishing to know this, the seer asked about his nature, and, told by those he asked that he is easy to reach, he saw the rest of the hymn for reaching Indra.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 5.30.2, at [383,2]). Sāyaṇa on 5.30.2 closes his gloss: though Indra exists, if hard to reach he is not to be approached; wishing to know this, the seer asked about his nature, was told he is easy to reach, and saw the rest of the hymn for reaching Indra. The sentence carries exactly that (‘sees the rest of the hymn’ is the seer’s seeing of a hymn, apaśyat). Plain sense faithful: 5.30.1 asks where the hero is and who has seen Indra, and 5.30.2 is the singer’s account of seeing, seeking and asking. Wilson’s rendering of 5.30.2 agrees.
